messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased container crashloop rate for service=redwood-infer-runtime-eu (node pool=inf-eu-west). Symptom: repeated CUDA OOMs + quick autoscaler spin-up/down. Auto-created thread 1768523456.

sre_oncall: saw the pager, joining. Any customer-facing impact?

support_ana: getting multiple CS tickets reporting timeouts for chat endpoints (user-facing errors ~503). Ticket count up ~12 in last 20m.

runtime_lead: quick summary from logs: when the autoscaler expands, new nodes come up with mixed GPU driver versions; some pods pick up a kernel path that causes driver resets -> CUDA OOMs, container restarts, then HPA sees lower utilization and kills nodes -> rapid scale down -> backlog -> repeat.

infra_engineer: attaching short log snippet:
```
[kernel] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3a:00.0: RmInitAdapter() failed: -6
runtime: panic: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
containerd: start failed: exit code 137
```

runtime_lead: reproduction pattern: burst of small requests triggers burst scaling policy (scale_up: 30 nodes / 5m), then cache warms, per-GPU qdepth drops and autoscaler removes nodes. The workload has a hotpath that benefits from PV cache on long-lived nodes; churn is killing cache and KV state, increasing per-request memory when reloading large models.

sre_oncall: immediate mitigation options?

infra_engineer: proposals: 1) temporarily disable aggressive scale_up burst (set max_surge to 8), 2) pin node image to stable gpu-driver v510, 3) cordon and drain nodes in erring AZ slowly, 4) enable fallback to quantized model variant. Which order?

runtime_lead: do 1 + 4 first (fast), then 2+3 if needed. Fallback reduces memory pressure immediately. I'll push a routing rule to route new sessions to model=redwood-lite-8q where possible.

sre_oncall: do it. @deploy_bot can you apply the rollout?

deploy_bot: starting rollout: applying route override -> route: inference/* -> model=redwood-lite-8q (canary 100% for new sessions) - change id d5f3e. ETA 45s.

sre_oncall: done, confirm traffic shift?

deploy_bot: rollout complete, all new sessions to redwood-lite-8q.

support_ana: early signs: error rate for chat endpoints dropping from 12% -> 4% over 6 minutes. Customers with long-running sessions still impacted.

pm_claire: any particular big customers affected?

customer_ops: two enterprise customers on dedicated pools reported degraded latency. They are onced on support. Reached out with status note.

infra_engineer: changing autoscaler config now: patching cluster-autoscaler config map -> set max_scale_up 8, scale_down_unneeded_time 10m, and disable burst flag. Command:
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch cm ca-config --patch '{"data":{"maxScaleUp":"8","burstEnabled":"false"}}'
```

sre_oncall: applying cordon plan: cordon 3 nodes with repeated NVRM resets, drain with maxUnavailable=1. Will stagger to keep cache.

runtime_lead: note: while draining, set model evictionGracePeriod=120s to avoid killing inference worker mid-request.

infra_engineer: cordon/drain in progress (node ids: inf-eu-07, inf-eu-09, inf-eu-11). Drains show some pods in CrashLoopBackOff and can't terminate cleanly; manually deleting restartPolicy for those pods.

sre_oncall: monitoring metrics: GPU memory pressure down 35% after quantized fallback + autoscaler rate limit. Error rate trending down slowly.

support_ana: pushing CS update: "We're seeing degraded performance due to a runtime issue causing container restarts during capacity churn. We have applied a temporary fallback and are limiting autoscaling while we remediate. Expected improvement within 15-30m."

pm_claire: notify affected accounts with ETA and invite to escalation call if they need uninterrupted traffic.

runtime_lead: long-term fixes: 1) ensure node images include uniform NVIDIA driver + kernel pairing, 2) autoscaler smoothing policy to use historical 5m+ windows for burst avoidance, 3) warm pool (keep N spare nodes with preloaded models), 4) KV cache persistence across pod restarts. We'll schedule RFC.

sre_oncall: any reason not to keep fallback active until node image remediation is rolled out?

runtime_lead: fallback reduces quality slightly; recommend keep for next 24h while we patch images and validate.

infra_engineer: starting node image roll forward to pinned driver v510 on staging, will run canary on inf-eu-12. Command:
```
imagebuilder promote --pool inf-eu-west --image redwood-gpu:v510-stable --canary 1
```
deploy_bot: canary image promoted to inf-eu-12. Watching NVRM logs and pod health.

sre_oncall: quick checklist for postmortem: incident start, customer impact (tickets + metrics), root cause hypothesis (driver mismatch + autoscaler spin), mitigations (fallback, autoscaler rate limit, cordon, image pin), follow-ups (RFC, warm pool, cache persistence). I'll open incident page and assign owners.

support_ana: created support artifact with ticket refs and customer notes.

customer_ops: internal note: two enterprise customers asked for dedicated maintenance windows; ops pushing options.

runtime_lead: started an eval job to quantify quality delta of 8q fallback vs main model for high-value flows. Results ETA 6h.

sre_oncall: leaving the channel but monitoring. If error rate creeps up again, page the SRE rotation. Thanks all. :ok_hand:

incbot: Incident update: status=mitigated -> partial, reason=fallback+autoscaler throttling applied, next_update=1768527612.

pm_claire: thanks team. I'll draft customer comms for tomorrow morning summarizing root cause and remediation plan.

support_ana: closing immediate CS loop for now; will reopen if customers report further issues.

runtime_lead: follow-ups assigned: infra_engineer -> node image pinning + canary rollout, runtime_lead -> warm-pool RFC + KV persistence, pm_claire -> customer comms.

sre_oncall: last check: 503s down to baseline, GPU OOM alerts down to normal. Marking incident as "stabilized".

incbot: thread 1768523456 archived (user: sre_oncall)
